CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right finger pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Sharon Brooks is a 48-year-old female presenting with right index finger pain. Patient reports injury occurred on Sunday while skiing, approximately 4 days ago. She was attempting moguls when her ski strap caught on her finger, causing hyperextension and bending the finger backward. Patient has tried ice and ibuprofen with minimal relief. Pain is exacerbated by movement.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies pain with passive range of motion testing. Able to flex, extend, and touch thumb with affected finger.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Constipation
Appendectomy at age 18

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for constipation
Ibuprofen (over-the-counter)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is an active individual who participates in skiing.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right index finger: Tenderness over distal phalanx and distal interphalangeal joint. No tenderness over proximal interphalangeal joint or metacarpophalangeal joint. Pain with finger flexion. Full range of motion maintained. No deformity appreciated.

RESULTS
Right index finger X-ray: No fractures identified. Normal alignment. All structures intact.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right index finger contusion, tip of finger. No fracture identified.
Plan: Aluminum foam splint for immobilization. Motrin 600 mg every 6 hours for approximately 1 week. Patient instructed to call and return if symptoms do not improve. Patient to follow up as needed.
